title: Contract validator
why: The ten checks, among them the mean drift that reports a possible unit change.
content:
"""Validate a DataFrame against a DatasetContract.

Pure pandas, no LLM. Every check runs, even after an earlier one fails,
so the report lists all violations at once.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pandas as pd

from churn_pipeline.contract.duplicates import duplicate_counts
from churn_pipeline.contract.models import ColumnSpec, DatasetContract


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Violation:
    check: str
    column: str | None
    expected: Any
    actual: Any
    message: str

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)


def file_sha256(path: str | Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 16), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def validate_against_contract(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    contract: DatasetContract,
    file_path: str | Path | None = None,
) -> list[Violation]:
    """Return every way df disagrees with contract; empty list means it passes.

    file_path, when given, is hashed and compared with contract.dataset.sha256.
    """
    violations: list[Violation] = []
    violations += _check_columns(df, contract)
    for spec in contract.columns:
        if spec.name in df.columns:
            violations += _check_column(df[spec.name], spec, contract)
    violations += _check_dataset(df, contract)
    if file_path is not None and contract.dataset.sha256:
        actual = file_sha256(file_path)
        if actual != contract.dataset.sha256:
            violations.append(Violation(
                "sha256", None, contract.dataset.sha256, actual,
                f"{Path(file_path).name} has changed since the contract was written",
            ))
    return violations


def _check_columns(df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DatasetContract) -> list[Violation]:
    expected = [c.name for c in contract.columns]
    missing = [c for c in expected if c not in df.columns]
    extra = [c for c in df.columns if c not in expected]
    out = []
    for name in missing:
        hint = f"; possible rename to one of {extra}" if extra else ""
        out.append(Violation("columns", name, "present", "missing",
                             f"column {name!r} is in the contract but not in the data{hint}"))
    for name in extra:
        out.append(Violation("columns", name, "absent", "present",
                             f"column {name!r} is in the data but not in the contract"))
    return out


def _check_column(s: pd.Series, spec: ColumnSpec, contract: DatasetContract) -> list[Violation]:
    out = []
    nulls = int(s.isna().sum())
    if nulls != spec.expected_null_count:
        out.append(Violation("nulls", spec.name, spec.expected_null_count, nulls,
                             f"{spec.name} has {nulls} missing values, contract expects {spec.expected_null_count}"))
    values = s.dropna()

    if spec.unique and s.duplicated().any():
        n = int(s.duplicated().sum())
        out.append(Violation("unique", spec.name, "unique", f"{n} duplicates",
                             f"{spec.name} must be unique but has {n} duplicate values"))

    if spec.dtype == "category":
        bad = sorted(set(values.astype(str)) - set(spec.allowed_values or []))
        if bad:
            out.append(Violation("allowed_values", spec.name, spec.allowed_values, bad,
                                 f"{spec.name} has values not allowed by the contract: {bad}"))
        return out

    if not pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(s) or pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(s):
        out.append(Violation("dtype", spec.name, spec.dtype, str(s.dtype),
                             f"{spec.name} should be numeric ({spec.dtype}) but is {s.dtype}"))
        return out
    if spec.dtype in ("int", "binary") and not (values == values.round()).all():
        out.append(Violation("dtype", spec.name, spec.dtype, "non-integer values",
                             f"{spec.name} should hold whole numbers but has fractional values"))
    if spec.dtype == "binary":
        bad = sorted(set(values.unique()) - {0, 1})
        if bad:
            out.append(Violation("allowed_values", spec.name, [0, 1], bad,
                                 f"{spec.name} is binary but has values {bad}"))

    if spec.range is not None and len(values):
        lo, hi = float(values.min()), float(values.max())
        if lo < spec.range.min or hi > spec.range.max:
            out.append(Violation("range", spec.name, [spec.range.min, spec.range.max], [lo, hi],
                                 f"{spec.name} ranges {lo:g}..{hi:g}, contract allows "
                                 f"{spec.range.min:g}..{spec.range.max:g}"))

    if spec.expected_mean is not None and len(values):
        out += _check_mean(spec, float(values.mean()), contract)
    return out


def _check_mean(spec: ColumnSpec, mean: float, contract: DatasetContract) -> list[Violation]:
    expected = spec.expected_mean
    assert expected is not None
    tol = contract.tolerances
    if expected == 0:
        drift = abs(mean)
    else:
        drift = abs(mean - expected) / abs(expected)
    if drift <= tol.mean_rel:
        return []
    message = (f"{spec.name} mean is {mean:,.2f}, contract expects {expected:,.2f} "
               f"(±{tol.mean_rel:.0%})")
    if expected != 0 and mean != 0:
        ratio = max(abs(mean / expected), abs(expected / mean))
        if ratio >= tol.unit_change_factor:
            unit = f" (contract unit: {spec.unit})" if spec.unit else ""
            message += f"; about {ratio:,.0f}x off, possible unit change{unit}"
    return [Violation("mean_drift", spec.name, expected, round(mean, 4), message)]


def _check_dataset(df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DatasetContract) -> list[Violation]:
    out = []
    expected_rows = contract.dataset.row_count
    if len(df) != expected_rows:
        out.append(Violation("row_count", None, expected_rows, len(df),
                             f"data has {len(df)} rows, contract expects {expected_rows}"))
    t = contract.target
    if t.name in df.columns and pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(df[t.name]):
        y = df[t.name].dropna()
        if len(y):
            rate = float((y == t.positive_class).mean())
            if abs(rate - t.expected_rate) > t.expected_rate * contract.tolerances.target_rate_rel:
                out.append(Violation("target_rate", t.name, t.expected_rate, round(rate, 4),
                                     f"{t.name} positive rate is {rate:.4f}, contract expects "
                                     f"{t.expected_rate:.4f} (±{contract.tolerances.target_rate_rel:.0%})"))
    out += _check_duplicates(df, contract)
    return out


def _check_duplicates(df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DatasetContract) -> list[Violation]:
    info = contract.dataset
    if info.duplicate_rows_ignoring_id is None and info.rows_in_duplicate_groups is None:
        return []
    ids = [c.name for c in contract.columns if c.role == "id" and c.name in df.columns]
    actual = duplicate_counts(df, ids)
    out = []
    if info.duplicate_rows_ignoring_id is not None \
            and actual["duplicate_rows_ignoring_id"] != info.duplicate_rows_ignoring_id:
        out.append(Violation("duplicates", None, info.duplicate_rows_ignoring_id,
                             actual["duplicate_rows_ignoring_id"],
                             f"data has {actual['duplicate_rows_ignoring_id']} rows that repeat another row "
                             f"under a new id, contract expects {info.duplicate_rows_ignoring_id}"))
    if info.rows_in_duplicate_groups is not None \
            and actual["rows_in_duplicate_groups"] != info.rows_in_duplicate_groups:
        out.append(Violation("duplicates", None, info.rows_in_duplicate_groups,
                             actual["rows_in_duplicate_groups"],
                             f"data has {actual['rows_in_duplicate_groups']} rows with an exact or "
                             f"one-value-different copy, contract expects {info.rows_in_duplicate_groups}"))
    return out

title: Duplicate detection
why: Rows repeated under a new id, exactly or with one value changed.
content:
"""Duplicate rows once the id column is ignored.

The dataset repeats customers under new ids: some rows are exact copies,
others copies with one value changed. Rows are grouped when they are equal
on every column, or on every column but one. The validator checks the
counts, and the Data Scientist Crew keeps each group on one side of the
train/test split so the test set never holds a copy of a training row.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def _row_keys(df: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
    return pd.util.hash_pandas_object(df, index=False).to_numpy()


def duplicate_groups(df: pd.DataFrame, id_columns: list[str]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Group label per row: rows equal on all columns, or all but one, share a label."""
    data = df.drop(columns=id_columns).reset_index(drop=True)
    parent = np.arange(len(data))

    def find(i: int) -> int:
        while parent[i] != i:
            parent[i] = parent[parent[i]]
            i = parent[i]
        return i

    for skip in [None, *data.columns]:
        keys = _row_keys(data if skip is None else data.drop(columns=[skip]))
        first: dict[int, int] = {}
        for i, k in enumerate(keys):
            if k in first:
                parent[find(i)] = find(first[k])
            else:
                first[k] = i
    return np.array([find(i) for i in range(len(data))])


def duplicate_counts(df: pd.DataFrame, id_columns: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    data = df.drop(columns=id_columns)
    sizes = pd.Series(duplicate_groups(df, id_columns)).value_counts()
    exact = data.duplicated(keep=False)
    counts = {
        # rows that repeat an earlier row exactly (the first copy is not counted)
        "duplicate_rows_ignoring_id": int(data.duplicated().sum()),
        "rows_with_an_exact_copy": int(exact.sum()),
        # groups of rows equal on all columns, or all but one
        "duplicate_groups": int((sizes > 1).sum()),
        "rows_in_duplicate_groups": int(sizes[sizes > 1].sum()),
        "largest_duplicate_group": int(sizes.max()),
    }
    # One sentence built in code, so agents quote it instead of combining the counts.
    counts["summary"] = (
        f"{counts['rows_with_an_exact_copy']:,} rows are exact copies of another row except for "
        f"their id ({counts['duplicate_rows_ignoring_id']:,} of them repeat an earlier row under a "
        f"new id). Counting copies with one value changed as well, "
        f"{counts['rows_in_duplicate_groups']:,} rows form {counts['duplicate_groups']:,} groups of "
        f"at most {counts['largest_duplicate_group']} rows, each row with its own id."
    )
    return counts

title: Training and evaluation
why: Features from the contract, the grouped split and the model comparison.
content:
"""Deterministic tools for the Data Scientist Crew.

The crew's only inputs are clean_data.csv and dataset_contract.json from
Crew 1. Agents decide and explain; these functions compute. Each public
function is plain Python (tested without an LLM) and has a thin CrewAI
@tool wrapper at the bottom of the file.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import joblib
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from crewai.tools import tool
from sklearn.base import clone
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier, RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance
from sklearn.metrics import (
    average_precision_score,
    confusion_matrix,
    precision_score,
    recall_score,
    roc_auc_score,
)
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedGroupKFold, cross_val_score

from churn_pipeline.contract.duplicates import duplicate_counts, duplicate_groups
from churn_pipeline.contract.models import DatasetContract, load_contract
from churn_pipeline.contract.validator import validate_against_contract

# Team decisions for step 4: two model families that handle missing values
# natively (no imputation); an 80/20 split stratified on the target with a
# fixed seed, where each group of duplicate rows stays on one side (one fold
# of five is the test set); and the minimum quality the step 5 gate enforces.
RANDOM_STATE = 42
CV_FOLDS = 5
THRESHOLD = 0.5
QUALITY_THRESHOLDS = {"pr_auc": 0.80, "recall": 0.60}
ONE_HOT_SEP = "="
GROUP_COLUMN = "duplicate_group"


def _write_json(path: Path, payload: Any) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def _r(x: float, ndigits: int = 4) -> float:
    return round(float(x), ndigits)


def _models() -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "hist_gradient_boosting": HistGradientBoostingClassifier(random_state=RANDOM_STATE),
        "random_forest": RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=300, random_state=RANDOM_STATE, n_jobs=-1),
    }


def _load_inputs(input_dir: str | Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, DatasetContract, Path]:
    input_dir = Path(input_dir)
    path = input_dir / "clean_data.csv"
    return pd.read_csv(path), load_contract(input_dir / "dataset_contract.json"), path


# ----------------------------------------------------------- contract review

def review_contract(input_dir: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate clean_data.csv against dataset_contract.json and list what modeling may use."""
    df, contract, path = _load_inputs(input_dir)
    violations = validate_against_contract(df, contract, file_path=path)
    ids = [c.name for c in contract.columns if c.role == "id"]
    features = [c for c in contract.columns
                if c.role == "feature" and c.name not in contract.forbidden_features]
    return {
        "contract_version": contract.contract_version,
        "rows": int(len(df)),
        "duplicate_rows_ignoring_id": contract.dataset.duplicate_rows_ignoring_id,
        "rows_in_duplicate_groups": contract.dataset.rows_in_duplicate_groups,
        "duplicates_summary": duplicate_counts(df, ids)["summary"],
        "passes": not violations,
        "violations": [v.to_dict() for v in violations],
        "target": {"name": contract.target.name, "expected_rate": contract.target.expected_rate},
        "forbidden_features": contract.forbidden_features,
        "features": [
            {"name": c.name, "dtype": c.dtype, "unit": c.unit, "unit_source": c.unit_source,
             "expected_null_count": c.expected_null_count,
             "allowed_values": c.allowed_values}
            for c in features
        ],
        "assumptions": contract.assumptions,
        "leakage_notes": contract.leakage_notes,
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------- features

def build_features(input_dir: str | Path, output_dir: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Write features.csv: id, duplicate group, target and model features from the contract.

    Numeric features are copied unchanged, missing values included. Each
    category column becomes one 0/1 column per allowed value in the contract,
    so different spellings stay separate. duplicate_group is not a feature:
    it keeps copies of a row on one side of the train/test split. Refuses to
    run when the data does not match the contract.
    """
    df, contract, path = _load_inputs(input_dir)
    violations = validate_against_contract(df, contract, file_path=path)
    if violations:
        raise ValueError("clean_data.csv does not match dataset_contract.json: "
                         + "; ".join(v.message for v in violations))

    id_cols = [c.name for c in contract.columns if c.role == "id"]
    target = contract.target.name
    out = df[id_cols + [target]].copy()
    out.insert(len(id_cols), GROUP_COLUMN, duplicate_groups(df, id_cols))
    sources = []
    for spec in contract.columns:
        if spec.role != "feature" or spec.name in contract.forbidden_features:
            continue
        if spec.dtype == "category":
            created = []
            for value in spec.allowed_values or []:
                name = f"{spec.name}{ONE_HOT_SEP}{value}"
                out[name] = (df[spec.name].astype(str) == value).astype(int)
                created.append(name)
            sources.append({"source": spec.name, "encoding": "one-hot", "columns": created})
        else:
            out[spec.name] = df[spec.name]
            sources.append({"source": spec.name, "encoding": "unchanged",
                            "missing_kept": int(df[spec.name].isna().sum())})

    feature_columns = [c for c in out.columns if c not in id_cols + [GROUP_COLUMN, target]]
    group_sizes = out[GROUP_COLUMN].value_counts()
    output_dir = Path(output_dir)
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.to_csv(output_dir / "features.csv", index=False)
    summary = {
        "output": str(output_dir / "features.csv"),
        "rows": int(len(out)),
        "id_columns": id_cols,
        "group_column": GROUP_COLUMN,
        "duplicate_groups": int((group_sizes > 1).sum()),
        "rows_in_duplicate_groups": int(group_sizes[group_sizes > 1].sum()),
        "target": target,
        "feature_count": len(feature_columns),
        "feature_columns": feature_columns,
        "missing_values_kept": int(out[feature_columns].isna().sum().sum()),
        "excluded": contract.forbidden_features,
        "sources": sources,
    }
    _write_json(output_dir / "feature_spec.json", summary)
    return summary


# --------------------------------------------------------- train & evaluate

def _test_metrics(y: pd.Series, proba: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, Any]:
    pred = (proba >= THRESHOLD).astype(int)
    tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y, pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
    return {
        "pr_auc": _r(average_precision_score(y, proba)),
        "recall": _r(recall_score(y, pred, zero_division=0)),
        "precision": _r(precision_score(y, pred, zero_division=0)),
        "roc_auc": _r(roc_auc_score(y, proba)),
        "confusion_matrix": {"tn": int(tn), "fp": int(fp), "fn": int(fn), "tp": int(tp)},
    }


def split_indices(data: pd.DataFrame, spec: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Train and test row positions of features.csv: stratified on the target, one fold of
    five as the test set, each duplicate group on one side. Deterministic."""
    cv = StratifiedGroupKFold(n_splits=CV_FOLDS, shuffle=True, random_state=RANDOM_STATE)
    return next(cv.split(data[spec["feature_columns"]], data[spec["target"]], data[spec["group_column"]]))


def train_and_evaluate(output_dir: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Train both models on features.csv, pick one by cross-validated PR-AUC, evaluate on test.

    Copies of a row never sit on both sides of a split, in the test split or
    in cross-validation. The model is chosen on the training split only; the
    test split is used once, after the choice, so test scores are an honest
    estimate. Writes model.joblib and evaluation_metrics.json.
    """
    output_dir = Path(output_dir)
    spec = json.loads((output_dir / "feature_spec.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    data = pd.read_csv(output_dir / "features.csv")
    X, y, groups = data[spec["feature_columns"]], data[spec["target"]], data[spec["group_column"]]
    cv = StratifiedGroupKFold(n_splits=CV_FOLDS, shuffle=True, random_state=RANDOM_STATE)
    train_idx, test_idx = split_indices(data, spec)
    X_train, X_test = X.iloc[train_idx], X.iloc[test_idx]
    y_train, y_test = y.iloc[train_idx], y.iloc[test_idx]
    shared_groups = len(set(groups.iloc[train_idx]) & set(groups.iloc[test_idx]))

    candidates = {}
    fitted = {}
    for name, model in _models().items():
        scores = cross_val_score(clone(model), X_train, y_train, groups=groups.iloc[train_idx],
                                 cv=cv, scoring="average_precision")
        model.fit(X_train, y_train)
        fitted[name] = model
        candidates[name] = {
            "cv_pr_auc_mean": _r(scores.mean()),
            "cv_pr_auc_std": _r(scores.std()),
            "test": _test_metrics(y_test, model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]),
        }
    selected = max(candidates, key=lambda n: candidates[n]["cv_pr_auc_mean"])
    best = fitted[selected]

    imp = permutation_importance(best, X_test, y_test, scoring="average_precision",
                                 n_repeats=5, random_state=RANDOM_STATE, n_jobs=-1)
    order = np.argsort(imp.importances_mean)[::-1][:10]
    top = [{"feature": X.columns[i], "pr_auc_drop": _r(imp.importances_mean[i])} for i in order]

    joblib.dump({"model": best, "model_name": selected, "feature_columns": spec["feature_columns"],
                 "target": spec["target"], "threshold": THRESHOLD}, output_dir / "model.joblib")
    test = candidates[selected]["test"]
    metrics = {
        "split": {"method": f"StratifiedGroupKFold({CV_FOLDS}), first fold is the test set",
                  "stratified_on": spec["target"], "grouped_by": spec["group_column"],
                  "random_state": RANDOM_STATE,
                  "train_rows": int(len(X_train)), "test_rows": int(len(X_test)),
                  "test_share": _r(len(X_test) / len(X)),
                  "train_churn_rate": _r(y_train.mean()), "test_churn_rate": _r(y_test.mean()),
                  "duplicate_groups_on_both_sides": shared_groups},
        "selection_rule": (f"highest mean PR-AUC over {CV_FOLDS}-fold stratified group CV "
                           "on the training split"),
        "threshold": THRESHOLD,
        "baseline_pr_auc": _r(y_test.mean()),
        "candidates": candidates,
        "selected_model": selected,
        "selected_test_metrics": test,
        "quality_thresholds": QUALITY_THRESHOLDS,
        "meets_quality_thresholds": all(test[k] >= v for k, v in QUALITY_THRESHOLDS.items()),
        "top_features_by_permutation": top,
        "model_file": str(output_dir / "model.joblib"),
    }
    _write_json(output_dir / "evaluation_metrics.json", metrics)
    return metrics


def read_model_facts(input_dir: str | Path, output_dir: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Everything the model card needs: contract text, feature summary and metrics."""
    df, contract, _ = _load_inputs(input_dir)
    ids = [c.name for c in contract.columns if c.role == "id"]
    output_dir = Path(output_dir)
    return {
        "contract_version": contract.contract_version,
        "dataset": contract.dataset.model_dump(),
        "target": contract.target.model_dump(),
        "duplicates_summary": duplicate_counts(df, ids)["summary"],
        "assumed_units": {c.name: c.unit for c in contract.columns if c.unit_source == "assumed"},
        "assumptions": contract.assumptions,
        "leakage_notes": contract.leakage_notes,
        "features": json.loads((output_dir / "feature_spec.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
        "metrics": json.loads((output_dir / "evaluation_metrics.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
    }


# ------------------------------------------------------- CrewAI tool wrappers

@tool("review_contract")
def review_contract_tool(input_dir: str) -> str:
    """Validate input_dir/clean_data.csv against input_dir/dataset_contract.json.
    Returns as JSON whether it passes, every violation, the target, the usable
    features with units, the forbidden features, assumptions and leakage notes."""
    return json.dumps(review_contract(input_dir), ensure_ascii=False)


@tool("build_features")
def build_features_tool(input_dir: str, output_dir: str) -> str:
    """Build output_dir/features.csv from input_dir/clean_data.csv using only the contract:
    numeric features unchanged (missing values kept), one 0/1 column per allowed category
    value. Refuses if the data does not match the contract. Returns the feature summary as JSON."""
    return json.dumps(build_features(input_dir, output_dir), ensure_ascii=False)


@tool("train_and_evaluate")
def train_and_evaluate_tool(output_dir: str) -> str:
    """Train HistGradientBoosting and RandomForest on output_dir/features.csv (80/20 split,
    stratified, duplicate rows kept on one side), select one by cross-validated PR-AUC on the
    training split, evaluate it on the test split against the quality thresholds and save
    model.joblib. Returns all metrics as JSON."""
    return json.dumps(train_and_evaluate(output_dir), ensure_ascii=False)


@tool("read_model_facts")
def read_model_facts_tool(input_dir: str, output_dir: str) -> str:
    """Return as JSON everything a model card needs: the contract's dataset, target, a sentence
    describing the duplicate rows, assumed units, assumptions and leakage notes, the feature
    summary and the evaluation metrics."""
    return json.dumps(read_model_facts(input_dir, output_dir), ensure_ascii=False)

title: Briefing situations
why: Code decides which situations apply and what the RAG searches for.
content:
"""Deterministic tools for the retention briefing.

customer_risk_profile scores one customer with the approved churn model and
returns the facts a briefing may quote. Like the playbook says, it refuses to
score anything unless the latest pipeline run passed every gate.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import joblib
import pandas as pd
from crewai.tools import tool

from churn_pipeline.news import news_query, search_recent_news
from churn_pipeline.tools.scientist_tools import split_indices

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
CREW1 = ROOT / "artifacts" / "latest" / "crew1"
CREW2 = ROOT / "artifacts" / "latest" / "crew2"
REPORT = ROOT / "artifacts" / "latest" / "validation_report.md"

# Risk bands from knowledge/harbor_vale/retention_playbook.md ("Who we contact first").
HIGH_RISK = 0.70
MEDIUM_RISK = 0.40


def require_approved_model(crew2_dir: str | Path = CREW2, report_path: str | Path = REPORT) -> None:
    """Raise unless the last run approved the model and its validation report says PASSED."""
    report = Path(report_path)
    if not (Path(crew2_dir) / "model_approved.json").is_file():
        raise ValueError("no approved model: the last pipeline run did not pass the quality gate")
    if not report.is_file() or "**PASSED**" not in report.read_text(encoding="utf-8"):
        raise ValueError(f"the latest validation report ({report.name}) does not say PASSED")


# The attributes a briefing shows, in this order; the rest stay in the tool output.
KEY_FACTS = ["Tenure", "Complain", "PreferredPaymentMode", "PreferedOrderCat", "SatisfactionScore",
             "DaySinceLastOrder", "OrderCount", "CashbackAmount"]


def risk_band(score: float) -> str:
    return "high" if score >= HIGH_RISK else "medium" if score >= MEDIUM_RISK else "low"


def situations(band: str, attributes: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """What applies to this customer, each with the search query that finds its policy.

    Built in code so the briefing always looks up the rules that matter
    (a complaint, a new customer, cash on delivery), not whatever the agent
    happens to search for.
    """
    out = [{"situation": f"{band} churn risk",
            "query": f"who we contact first and which channel for {band} risk customers"}]
    tenure = attributes.get("Tenure")
    # The playbook's new-customer rule covers customers the model flagged, not low-risk ones.
    if tenure is not None and tenure <= 1 and band != "low":
        out.append({"situation": "new customer (tenure 0 to 1 months)",
                    "query": "new customers in their first months welcome call first contact discount"})
    if attributes.get("Complain") == 1:
        out.append({"situation": "complained in the last month",
                    "query": "customer complained coupon resolve before you reward"})
    if attributes.get("PreferredPaymentMode") in ("COD", "Cash on Delivery"):
        out.append({"situation": "pays cash on delivery",
                    "query": "cash on delivery customers cashback free delivery voucher"})
    category = attributes.get("PreferedOrderCat")
    if category in ("Mobile", "Mobile Phone"):
        out.append({"situation": f"prefers the {category} category",
                    "query": "competitor offers for phone buyers mobile category"})
    elif category == "Grocery":
        out.append({"situation": "prefers the Grocery category", "query": "discounts in the Grocery category"})
    if band != "low":
        out.append({"situation": "an offer may be made",
                    "query": "discount limits per customer and approval levels"})
    return out


def all_situation_queries() -> list[str]:
    """Every search query situations() can produce, for every band and attribute that matters."""
    queries: dict[str, None] = {}
    for band, tenure, complain, payment, category in itertools.product(
            ("high", "medium", "low"), (0, 5), (0, 1), ("COD", "UPI"), ("Mobile", "Grocery", "Fashion")):
        for s in situations(band, {"Tenure": tenure, "Complain": complain,
                                   "PreferredPaymentMode": payment, "PreferedOrderCat": category}):
            queries[s["query"]] = None
    return list(queries)


def _plain(v: Any) -> Any:
    """A JSON-friendly value: NaN becomes None, floats are rounded to 2 places."""
    if pd.isna(v):
        return None
    v = v.item() if hasattr(v, "item") else v
    return round(v, 2) if isinstance(v, float) else v


def all_customer_profiles(crew1_dir: str | Path = CREW1, crew2_dir: str | Path = CREW2,
                          report_path: str | Path = REPORT) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Score every customer at once, with the same rules as customer_risk_profile.

    The web app shows an instant briefing for any CustomerID from this table,
    so it needs neither scikit-learn nor the model file.
    """
    require_approved_model(crew2_dir, report_path)
    crew2_dir = Path(crew2_dir)
    bundle = joblib.load(crew2_dir / "model.joblib")
    spec = json.loads((crew2_dir / "feature_spec.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    metrics = json.loads((crew2_dir / "evaluation_metrics.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    features = pd.read_csv(crew2_dir / "features.csv")
    clean = pd.read_csv(Path(crew1_dir) / "clean_data.csv").set_index(spec["id_columns"][0])
    scores = bundle["model"].predict_proba(features[bundle["feature_columns"]])[:, 1]
    test = set(split_indices(features, spec)[1])

    customers = {}
    for i, (customer_id, score) in enumerate(zip(features[spec["id_columns"][0]], scores)):
        attributes = {c: _plain(v) for c, v in clean.loc[customer_id].items() if c != spec["target"]}
        band = risk_band(float(score))
        customers[str(int(customer_id))] = {
            "score": round(float(score), 2), "band": band, "out_of_sample": i in test,
            "facts": [attributes.get(c) for c in KEY_FACTS],
            "situations": [s["situation"] for s in situations(band, attributes)],
            "queries": [s["query"] for s in situations(band, attributes)],
        }
    return {"model": metrics["selected_model"], "key_facts": KEY_FACTS,
            "band_rule": {"high": HIGH_RISK, "medium": MEDIUM_RISK}, "customers": customers}


def customer_risk_profile(customer_id: int, crew1_dir: str | Path = CREW1, crew2_dir: str | Path = CREW2,
                          report_path: str | Path = REPORT) -> dict[str, Any]:
    require_approved_model(crew2_dir, report_path)
    crew2_dir = Path(crew2_dir)
    bundle = joblib.load(crew2_dir / "model.joblib")
    spec = json.loads((crew2_dir / "feature_spec.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    metrics = json.loads((crew2_dir / "evaluation_metrics.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    features = pd.read_csv(crew2_dir / "features.csv")
    clean = pd.read_csv(Path(crew1_dir) / "clean_data.csv")
    id_col = spec["id_columns"][0]

    rows = features.index[features[id_col] == int(customer_id)]
    if len(rows) == 0:
        raise ValueError(f"customer {customer_id} is not in the data")
    i = rows[0]
    score = float(bundle["model"].predict_proba(features.loc[[i], bundle["feature_columns"]])[:, 1][0])
    _, test_idx = split_indices(features, spec)

    raw = clean.loc[clean[id_col] == int(customer_id)].iloc[0]
    attributes = {c: (None if pd.isna(v) else
                      round(v.item(), 2) if isinstance(v.item() if hasattr(v, "item") else v, float) else
                      (v.item() if hasattr(v, "item") else v))
                  for c, v in raw.items() if c not in (id_col, spec["target"])}
    return {
        "customer_id": int(customer_id),
        "risk_score": round(score, 2),
        "risk_band": risk_band(score),
        "risk_band_rule": f"high >= {HIGH_RISK}, medium >= {MEDIUM_RISK}, otherwise low (retention playbook)",
        "scored_out_of_sample": bool(i in set(test_idx)),
        "score_note": ("the model never saw this customer during training"
                       if i in set(test_idx) else
                       "this customer was in the training data, so the score is optimistic about the model"),
        "key_facts": {c: attributes.get(c) for c in KEY_FACTS},
        "missing_facts": [c for c in KEY_FACTS if attributes.get(c) is None],
        "situations": situations(risk_band(score), attributes),
        "news_query": news_query(attributes.get("PreferedOrderCat")),
        "model": {"name": metrics["selected_model"], "test_pr_auc": metrics["selected_test_metrics"]["pr_auc"],
                  "test_recall": metrics["selected_test_metrics"]["recall"],
                  "top_features": [t["feature"] for t in metrics["top_features_by_permutation"][:5]]},
    }


@tool("customer_risk_profile")
def customer_risk_profile_tool(customer_id: int) -> str:
    """Score one customer (by CustomerID) with the approved churn model. Returns as JSON the risk
    score, the playbook's risk band, whether the score is out of sample, the customer's key facts
    (tenure in months, complaint flag, payment mode, preferred category and more), the situations
    that apply to the customer with a search query for each, and the model's test metrics.
    Refuses if the latest pipeline run did not pass every gate."""
    return json.dumps(customer_risk_profile(customer_id), ensure_ascii=False)


@tool("search_recent_news")
def search_recent_news_tool(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web for news from the last 48 hours (Google News, English-language news in the US).
    Pass the news_query from customer_risk_profile exactly as given. Returns JSON with up to five
    articles (title, url, source, published) newest first, or an error when the search failed."""
    return json.dumps(search_recent_news(query), ensure_ascii=False)

title: Web search
why: Market news from the last 48 hours through Google News RSS, without an API key.
content:
"""Web search for the latest market news, through Google News RSS (no API key).

The course brief asks the agent to search the web for news from the last 48
hours. Harbor & Vale is fictional, so the search covers a real market:
online retail in the United States, narrowed by the customer's preferred
category.

Google News serves search results as RSS without a key; `when:2d` limits them
to the last two days, and hl/gl/ceid pick English-language news for the US.
Articles older than 48 hours are dropped again here, in case the feed is
looser than the operator. Standard library and no crewai, so the web app can
use it too (the agent's tool wrapper lives in tools/briefing_tools.py).

A failed or slow search returns no articles and an error message, never an
exception: a briefing without news is still a briefing.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from email.utils import parsedate_to_datetime
from typing import Any

FEED_URL = "https://news.google.com/rss/search"
WINDOW = timedelta(hours=48)
MAX_ARTICLES = 5
TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 8
MAX_BYTES = 1_000_000
CACHE_SECONDS = 15 * 60
LOCALE = {"hl": "en-US", "gl": "US", "ceid": "US:en"}

# Market news query per preferred category, in Google search syntax.
CATEGORY_QUERIES = {
    "Mobile": "smartphone (sale OR discount OR deal)",
    "Mobile Phone": "smartphone (sale OR discount OR deal)",
    "Laptop & Accessory": "(laptop OR electronics) (sale OR discount OR deal)",
    "Fashion": "fashion (ecommerce OR \"online shopping\" OR sale)",
    "Grocery": "(\"online grocery\" OR \"grocery delivery\")",
}
DEFAULT_QUERY = "(ecommerce OR \"online shopping\") (discount OR sale OR deal)"

_cache: dict[str, tuple[float, dict[str, Any]]] = {}
# Every article link any search returned in this process. Google issues a new
# link token for the same article on each request, so a briefing's guardrail
# checks links against all of them, not just one search's.
SEEN_URLS: set[str] = set()


# The US edition of Google News still lists some Indian outlets; leave them out.
EXCLUDE = "-India -Rs"


def news_query(category: str | None) -> str:
    return f"{CATEGORY_QUERIES.get(category or '', DEFAULT_QUERY)} {EXCLUDE}"


def parse_feed(xml_text: str, now: datetime, max_articles: int = MAX_ARTICLES) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Articles from a Google News RSS document, newest first, within the 48-hour window."""
    articles = []
    for item in ET.fromstring(xml_text).iter("item"):
        try:
            published = parsedate_to_datetime(item.findtext("pubDate", ""))
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            continue
        if published.tzinfo is None:
            published = published.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        if not timedelta(0) <= now - published <= WINDOW:
            continue
        source = item.find("source")
        outlet = source.text.strip() if source is not None and source.text else ""
        title = item.findtext("title", "").strip()
        # Google appends " - Outlet" to every title; the outlet is shown separately.
        if outlet and title.endswith(f" - {outlet}"):
            title = title[: -len(f" - {outlet}")]
        articles.append({"title": title, "url": item.findtext("link", "").strip(), "source": outlet,
                         "published": published.astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC"),
                         "_at": published})
    articles.sort(key=lambda a: a["_at"], reverse=True)
    return [{k: v for k, v in a.items() if k != "_at"} for a in articles[:max_articles]]


def search_recent_news(query: str, max_articles: int = MAX_ARTICLES) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Articles Google News lists for query from the last 48 hours, newest first."""
    cached = _cache.get(query)
    if cached and time.time() - cached[0] < CACHE_SECONDS:
        return cached[1]
    url = f"{FEED_URL}?{urllib.parse.urlencode({'q': f'{query} when:2d', **LOCALE})}"
    result: dict[str, Any] = {"query": query, "window": "last 48 hours", "source": "Google News",
                              "articles": [], "error": None}
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (churn-pipeline course project)"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS) as response:
            body = response.read(MAX_BYTES).decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        result["articles"] = parse_feed(body, datetime.now(timezone.utc), max_articles)
        SEEN_URLS.update(a["url"] for a in result["articles"])
    except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, ET.ParseError, ValueError, OSError) as e:
        result["error"] = f"news search unavailable: {e}"
    if result["error"] is None:
        _cache[query] = (time.time(), result)
    return result

title: Briefing guardrail
why: A crew that refuses to start without an approved model, and checks every citation and link.

title: An agent's prompts
why: The Data Analyst crew's task prompts.
content:
inspect_raw_data_task:
  description: >
    Profile the raw dataset at {raw_data_path} (sheet "E Comm") with the
    profile_raw_data tool. The tool writes {output_dir}/quality_report.json.

    From the tool output, summarise for the team:
    - row count, duplicate rows and whether CustomerID is unique
    - duplicates once CustomerID is ignored: quote the tool's
      duplicates_ignoring_id.summary sentence word for word, then give the
      churn rate in duplicate groups. Do not combine the counts in your own
      words. Say plainly that "duplicate rows: 0" only holds because every
      row has its own id
    - every column with missing values: count, share, and churn rate when the
      value is missing versus present
    - every categorical column with each spelling, its count and churn rate,
      pointing out spellings that look like the same meaning; they are kept
      as separate categories because their churn rates differ, so report the
      difference without guessing its cause (do not call it a data-entry error)
    - numeric outliers the tool flagged
    - the overall churn rate

    Use only numbers that appear in the tool output. Do not recommend imputing,
    merging categories or clipping outliers: the team decided against all three.
  expected_output: >
    A markdown quality summary with sections Overview, Missing values,
    Categories, Outliers and Target, where every number matches
    quality_report.json.
  agent: data_quality_inspector
  output_file: "{output_dir}/quality_summary.md"

prepare_clean_data_task:
  description: >
    Create the handoff file with the export_clean_data tool: it reads sheet
    "E Comm" from {raw_data_path}, writes {output_dir}/clean_data.csv without
    changing any value, re-reads the CSV and compares it to the raw data cell by
    cell, and returns the comparison result and the file's sha256.

    The team decisions you must follow and document:
    - missing values stay missing (no imputation, no synthetic values)
    - category spellings stay as they are (no merging)
    - outliers stay as they are (no clipping or removal)

    If the tool reports any difference between the CSV and the raw data, say
    so plainly at the top of the log and do not describe the file as faithful.
  expected_output: >
    A markdown preparation log with sections Source, Steps, Decisions,
    Verification (the tool's comparison result and the sha256) and Output.
  agent: data_preparation_engineer
  context:
    - inspect_raw_data_task
  output_file: "{output_dir}/preparation_log.md"

eda_task:
  description: >
    Run the run_eda tool on {output_dir}/clean_data.csv. It writes
    {output_dir}/eda_report.html with descriptive statistics, distributions and
    churn-rate charts, and returns the computed churn rates by group.

    Then write business insights for Harbor & Vale's retention team:
    - which customer groups churn most, with their size and churn rate
    - what that means for where the discount budget should go
    - spellings that look like the same meaning (for example COD and Cash on
      Delivery): they are kept as separate categories because their churn
      rates differ; report both rates and do not guess the cause (do not call
      it a data-entry error or say the groups behave the same)
    - missing values whose churn rate differs from present values
    - rows repeated under a new CustomerID: quote the tool's
      duplicates_ignoring_id sentence word for word (do not combine the counts
      in your own words), and say that every copy is counted as a separate
      customer in the group sizes and churn rates above
    - SatisfactionScore and the other score columns have no documented
      direction (the data dictionary does not say whether 5 is best or
      worst), so name the score value (for example "score 5"), never "lowest"
      or "highest" satisfaction
    - the known limitation that the churn window is undefined, so last-month
      columns may describe customers after they churned

    Quote only numbers the tool returned. Do not claim causation.
  expected_output: >
    A markdown insights document with an executive summary of three to five
    bullet points, then sections Who churns, Budget implications, Data caveats.
  agent: eda_insights_analyst
  context:
    - inspect_raw_data_task
    - prepare_clean_data_task
  output_file: "{output_dir}/insights.md"

publish_contract_task:
  description: >
    Use the build_contract tool on {output_dir}/clean_data.csv. It computes
    every number of the contract (types, ranges, means, null counts, allowed
    values, row count, target rate, sha256) and returns the column list.

    Your part is the text the tool cannot know. Return:
    - a one-sentence description for every column, based on the data
      dictionary sheet "Data Dict" in {raw_data_path} and the tool output
    - the assumptions the Data Scientist crew must know: no imputation, no
      category merging, outliers kept, duplicate rows kept (rows repeated
      under a new CustomerID, exactly or with one value changed; counts are in
      the tool output under dataset), and which units are assumed
      (Tenure in months, WarehouseToHome in km, CashbackAmount in INR)
    - leakage notes: the churn window is undefined, so Complain, CouponUsed,
      OrderCount, CashbackAmount and PreferedOrderCat (all "last month") may
      leak; the different spellings with different churn rates; and the
      duplicate rows, which leak between train and test unless each group of
      copies stays on one side of the split

    Do not return or change any number; the code merges your text with the
    tool's numbers into {output_dir}/dataset_contract.json.
  expected_output: >
    Column descriptions for all 20 columns, a list of assumptions and a list of
    leakage notes, in the structured format requested.
  agent: contract_steward
  context:
    - inspect_raw_data_task
    - prepare_clean_data_task
